prose_changes.old: In April 1913, at the Arroyo Seco camp meeting, R. E. McAlister preached on baptism and observed that the baptisms recorded in Acts are performed in the name of Jesus. The following year Frank Ewart and Glenn Cook baptized one another on that basis, and the question tore through the young Pentecostal movement. In October 1916 the Assemblies of God adopted its Statement of Fundamental Truths, an explicitly trinitarian confession, and the ministers who could not sign it left — so the rupture stands documented in each side's own words. Several bodies followed. The Pentecostal Assemblies of the World is the oldest, Oneness from 1916, and was interracial through decades in which other Pentecostal bodies separated by race; the separations of 1924, and the racial dimension of the 1945 merger, are part of its own telling, and G. T. Haywood was among its leaders. The United Pentecostal Church International was formed by a merger vote on 25 September 1945 and published its Articles of Faith in a Manual reissued each year. In Mexico the Apostolic revival began in 1914. Romanita Carbajal de Valenzuela had become a Pentecostal in Los Angeles, and that year she returned to Villa Aldama in Chihuahua. The Iglesia Apostólica de la Fe en Cristo Jesús grew from it.
